newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa-UAP shareholders' equity 70 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Axa-UAP shareholders' equity 70 bln Ffr.

text.p: Shareholders' equity of the new merged Axa-UAP insurance group is expected to total around 70 billion francs ($12.3 billion) after harmonisation of their accounts, Gerard de la Martiniere, senior vice-president of the group, said on Wednesday.
"Our estimate is that we could end up with shareholders' equity for the total Axa-UAP of 70 billion francs," he told a news conference at which the group's results were announced.
He said that the amount could not be determined exactly until the accounting methods of UAP and Axa were made to conform.
The group's treasury will total 47 billion francs.
Its consolidated debt was 36 billion francs, of which half belonged to U.S. insurance unit The Equitable.
Henri de Castries, another senior vice president, said that since the start of 1997 Axa-UAP had sold 4.5 billion francs of assets.
Shareholders of Axa and UAP are due to vote on the merger in May.
